_doc: Curated technique seeds (knowledge_architecture.md section 5), one file per area. Fields: id, level + scope (a scope node or universal), aliases (v1 / technique-DB / footer names folded in), mechanism, preconditions (predicate DSL), predicts (canonical metric -> up|down|flat|up_or_flat|down_or_flat), risks (pitfalls), states / op_classes / op_kinds gates (empty = any), slot (offered by the multi-slot agent), prior {mean, n}: a seed prior with a low pseudo-count that evidence overrides, realizations by scope (target:<key> | target:<backend>:sm_NN+ | target:<backend> | node:<id> | universal). Loaded by Ontology.seed(); scripts/seed_knowledge.py builds a knowledge.db from these files.

techniques.mechanism: matrix units execute a whole 16x16xK multiply-accumulate per instruction, far above the scalar FMA ceiling
risks: fp16/tf32 inputs exceed fp32 tolerances (1e-3 relative with K >= 1024 often fails)
bf16 tensor cores need sm_80+; on sm_75 a bf16 slot computes in fp32 (bf16 -> fp16 is exact only inside fp16's range)
M/N/K not multiples of 16: pad tiles in on-chip memory

realizations.how: nvcuda::wmma 16x16x16 fragments with fp16 inputs and fp32 accumulators (sm_75: fp16 only; for fp32 problems only if the tolerance allows rounding inputs to fp16 -- usually it does not for K >= 1024; bf16 problems: no bf16 tensor cores on sm_75, compute in fp32).

wmma::precision::tf32 (m16n16k8) or mma.sync bf16/tf32 with fp32 accumulators; tf32 keeps 10 mantissa bits, check the tolerance. bf16 problems: wmma 16x16x16 / mma.sync m16n8k16 on __nv_bfloat16 inputs with fp32 accumulators -- the products of bf16 inputs are exact, so only the fp32 accumulation order differs from the reference.
wgmma (warpgroup MMA, asynchronous) fed by TMA; see tma_wgmma_pipeline.

techniques.mechanism: ldmatrix loads tensor-core fragments from shared memory in the layout mma expects, one instruction per 8x8 sub-matrix set

realizations.how: ldmatrix.sync.aligned.m8n8.x4 from a swizzled shared tile into mma.sync operands (sm_75+).

techniques.mechanism: asynchronous global->shared copies (no register staging) in a 3-4 stage ring buffer keep the tensor / FMA units fed
risks: wrong wait_group counts read stale stages
on-chip memory per stage limits occupancy

realizations.how: cp.async.cg.shared.global 16-byte copies per stage, cp.async.commit_group / wait_group<stages-2>, __syncthreads between stages; Ampere / Ada only (no realization on sm_75).

techniques.mechanism: Hopper: TMA bulk tensor copies with mbarrier synchronisation feed asynchronous warpgroup MMAs
risks: descriptor setup (cuTensorMapEncodeTiled) is host-side; needs sm_90a

realizations.how: cp.async.bulk.tensor (TMA) into swizzled shared tiles, mbarrier arrive/wait per stage, wgmma.mma_async with a warpgroup of 128 threads.

techniques.mechanism: pad or swizzle shared-memory rows so a warp's accesses hit distinct banks instead of serialising

realizations.how: Pad on-chip tiles by one element per row (e.g. [32][33]) or XOR-swizzle the column index so lanes hit distinct banks.

techniques.mechanism: less on-chip memory per block (reuse buffers, right-sized dynamic allocation) so more blocks are resident

realizations.how: extern __shared__ sized per launch; reuse one buffer across phases; smaller tiles when occupancy is the limit; >48 KB needs cudaFuncSetAttribute(MaxDynamicSharedMemorySize).

techniques.mechanism: split a block into producer warps (loads) and consumer warps (math) synchronised by barriers, so memory and compute overlap without register staging
risks: complex synchronisation; only worth it on large tiled GEMM / attention

realizations.how: Producer warps issue cp.async / TMA into a stage ring, consumer warps wait on named barriers (bar.sync id) or mbarriers and run the MMAs.
